name: org.machanism.machai:ghostwriter
description: Machai Ghostwriter is a Java 8 project-wide AI-assisted documentation and maintenance engine. It scans source code, tests, Markdown and HTML site content, XML, TypeScript, Python, PlantUML diagrams, configuration, and other selected project files. In guidance mode it discovers embedded @guidance instructions or folder-level @guidance.txt instructions, uses format-aware reviewers to assemble file context, and sends bounded requests to a configured GenAI provider. In Act mode it executes reusable TOML-defined workflows with ordered episodes, inherited defaults, configurable scan scope, optional interactive follow-up, and controlled functional tools. Ghostwriter supports project-relative file reads and edits, approved command execution, web and REST access, shared project context, workflow control, configurable provider/model selection, glob and regular-expression paths, exclusions, module-aware traversal, and parallel processing. It is intended for repeatable local development and Maven or CI/CD automation that keeps code, tests, documentation, diagrams, and configuration aligned.

classification.type: CLI application and Maven-integrated automation library

features.name: Ghostwriter command-line entry point
features.signature: public static void main(java.lang.String[] args) throws java.io.IOException, org.apache.commons.cli.ParseException
features.description: Starts Ghostwriter. The entry point parses command-line options, loads persisted configuration, gives command-line values precedence, chooses guidance mode by default or Act mode when --act is present, invokes the appropriate processor, and maps recognized processing failures to JVM exit codes. Use --help to print usage without starting processing.

examples.snippet:
# 1. Build the CLI delivery artifact from the project root.
mvn -Ppack install

# 2. Configure the GenAI provider and model in gw.properties.
gw.model=CodeMie:your-model

# 3. Scan Markdown files whose embedded guidance describes the required update.
java -jar target/gw.jar "glob:**/*.md"
examples.description: Builds the Java CLI, configures a provider/model in the standard properties file, and runs guided processing for project Markdown files. Provider credentials and endpoint settings must be supplied through the configured provider mechanism rather than committed to source control.

examples.snippet:
# Run a reusable workflow against the current project.
java -jar target/gw.jar . --act unit-tests
examples.description: Invokes the built-in unit-tests Act. Acts are TOML-defined multi-step workflows that can inspect the project, use permitted tools, and perform repeatable maintenance work.

features.name: Guidance-driven file processing
features.description: Processes selected project files using instructions embedded near the content. Built-in reviewers recognize guidance in Java, Markdown, HTML/XML, TypeScript, Python, PlantUML, and the folder-level @guidance.txt convention. This is suited to durable, reviewable instructions that remain versioned with the artifact they govern.

examples.snippet:
<!-- @guidance:
Update this page for new users.
Preserve existing license details.
-->

# Then execute:
java -jar target/gw.jar "glob:src/site/**/*.md"
examples.description: Adds a Markdown guidance comment and runs a scoped scan. Ghostwriter finds the tag, prepares context for the matching file, and requests the configured AI-assisted update.

features.name: Act-driven workflows
features.description: Loads and executes named TOML Act definitions. An Act can define stable instructions, one or more ordered episodes, defaults, inheritance, scan settings, interactive behavior, and YAML-front-matter enabledTools rules. Tool patterns match fully qualified tool identifiers, allowing a workflow to restrict available capabilities or request automatic tool selection.

examples.snippet:
# acts/doc-audit.toml
description = "Review Markdown documentation."
instructions = "Explain recommendations clearly."
inputs = '''
---
enabledTools:
  - org\.machanism\..*:read_file
---
Review the selected documentation.
'''

[gw]
path = "glob:src/site/**/*.md"

# Invoke the configured Act.
java -jar target/gw.jar . --acts acts --act doc-audit
examples.description: Creates a custom documentation-review Act, limits it to read-file tools through a regular-expression rule, scopes it to site Markdown, and invokes it from the CLI.

examples.title: Install, configure, and run Ghostwriter in a Maven project
steps: Install Java 8 or newer and Maven 3.x.
Build the delivery artifact with mvn -Ppack install, or download and unpack the Ghostwriter CLI pack.
Create or update gw.properties with the configured GenAI provider, model, credentials, and endpoint required by that provider.
Add an @guidance instruction to a supported project file, describing the outcome and protected content.
Run java -jar target/gw.jar "glob:**/*.md" from the project root and review the generated changes before committing them.
examples.description: This scenario applies repeatable guidance-driven documentation maintenance to all Markdown files selected by a glob. Start with a narrow path before moving the command into CI/CD.

examples.title: Run an unattended reusable workflow
steps: Choose a built-in Act such as unit-tests or place a custom TOML Act in the configured acts directory.
Set its [gw] path, excludes, and tool permissions to the smallest scope that supports the task.
Inspect results, tests, and build output; then reuse the verified command in an automation job.
examples.description: Acts provide named, versionable workflows for multi-step automation. Non-interactive Acts are appropriate for routine jobs where all required settings are supplied beforehand.
